approval_note: Morning runs on or before this date open a pull request that goes live when the publisher merges it. Later runs publish to main by 06:00 themselves.

method_versions.label: Pilot and early editions: forecasts without a structured record of the forecasters
Five recorded forecasters, slip classes, interval claims, quotas on probability bands
Event window and evidence time, full record of forecasting steps (blind and after-market estimates), numbers derived from one distribution, no quotas on probabilities, coverage of missed events
Selection by news value: the biggest running stories of the day must be covered with a claim on their next step; economy desk with a minimum; photographs in every edition

Lessons from the first 132 resolved claims: results within 72 hours, poll models with a minimum error for elections, wider number ranges centred on consensus, data-direction claims only away from the threshold, calibration only when it helps out of sample, recorded market search, research when forecasters disagree, an outsider without the shared dossier

Honest measurement: a recorded state of the sources behind each edition, revisions that only confirm reported news kept out of the forecast score, event and case keys, a pre-stated baseline on every claim, an independent audit of a fixed sample of results, a history of surprises for number forecasts, and a joint simulation of linked races

newsletter._note: Morning edition by e-mail: the service reads /feed.xml (English) or /cs/feed.xml (Czech) and sends each new item. Set username to the Buttondown account name to show the sign-up form on the site.

_notes.election_lead_sd_min: Minimum sd (pp) of the top-two lead in the poll model, by level. Pooled poll error 2.7–3.6 pp (pipeline/reference-data/poll-error.json); our first 17 election claims scored Brier 0.265, so the floor sits at the upper end and above it for regional and local races, where polling is thinner.
_notes.interval_width_min_scales: q90 − q10 must be at least this many surprise scales: 1.6 × the Normal 80% width (2.56). Only 7 of our first 13 ranges held the result.
_notes.release_threshold_min_scales: A yes/no claim on a data release needs the threshold at least this many surprise scales from consensus; nearer, it is a coin toss: use an interval claim instead.
_notes.research_spread: If the five final estimates span more than this, a research agent looks for the disputed fact before freezing (spread ≥ 15 points scored 0.170 against 0.140).

_notes.audit_share: Share of results re-resolved by a separate agent that cannot see the recorded outcome. Fixed by hash in lib.mjs (auditSample).
_notes.source_access_min_share: Below this share of reference pages read, or of fact-check pages opened, the edition is marked as limited on its page.
_notes.single_analyst: The role named in advance as the single-analyst comparison from version 6. Chosen here on 2 November 2026 from the record to that date, so only editions of version 6 and later count as a fair test.
_notes.baseline_prior: Beta prior of the persistence baseline: the share of status-quo outcomes among results known before an edition's freeze.
_notes.backtest_min_test: A fitted stage goes live only after beating the plain ensemble by at least backtest_min_gain on this many later claims. On 2 November 2026 the correction led by 0.0035 on 38 claims, which proves nothing.

open_questions._note: Publisher's decision, 9 November 2026: about a third of all claims were 90% sure or more, and they flattered the score. The accuracy page and each edition's results lead with open questions (band); near-certain claims are shown apart. From edition `from` at most easy_main_max stories may lead with a claim of 90% or more (either way), and every other claim at or beyond sure_claim needs forecast.open_because, a sourced reason the question is genuinely open.
